sam_dev: Heads-up — during our sandbox ramp we see a weird mix: streaming responses (chat/stream) get 401 mid-stream, while embedding calls immediately return 429. Behavior is non-deterministic across workers. Anyone seen both together?
maria_cs: ugh — thanks for flagging. Can you share the auth flow and whether you rotate tokens frequently? Also how many concurrent connections do you open?
sam_dev: we mint very short lived tokens (TTL 45s) from our auth proxy. Each instance maintains an HTTP/2 pool and we do token refresh per-process, not per-request. Concurrency: ~60 streams + 30 embedding requests during warmup. Logs below (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-19T15:02:41Z] auth: POST /token -> 200 {"token":"ey..","expires_in":45}
[2026-03-19T15:02:42Z] stream-start -> 200 partial data
[2026-03-19T15:02:43Z] stream-chunk -> 401 {"error":"invalid_token"}
[2026-03-19T15:02:44Z] embeds -> 429 {"error":"rate_limit"}
[2026-03-19T15:02:44Z] embeds -> 429
```
sam_dev: note: stream requests sometimes succeed for ~2-10s then 401 mid-stream. Embeds are immediately 429.
nina_sre: interesting pattern. Two hypotheses: 1) token header bound to connection/HTTP2 stream and when you rotate token the connection still has old auth state; 2) our rate-limiter treats concurrent new downstream streams + token handshake traffic as a burst. With many long-lived HTTP/2 connections you can get cross-talk where a connection's metadata is stale. Did you use per-connection auth metadata or Authorization header per request?
sam_dev: we attach Authorization header per request, but we reuse connections so the TLS session is reused. Our proxy sometimes caches the initial header for performance.
maria_cs: that cache-on-reuse is key. For short TTL tokens your connection reuse + proxy-level header caching can lead to the server seeing an already-expired token or rejected token mid-stream after rotation. That would explain 401 mid-stream. Embeds hitting 429 suggests burst accounting — many embeddings + auth checks within the same burst window.
sdk-bot: recommend two changes you can try while we triage: 1) short-term: add a token-grace and force TLS connection reset after refresh (or disable connection reuse during warmup) for clients doing sub-1min tokens; 2) medium-term: coalesce refreshes (singleflight), and stagger warmup using jitter/backoff. Example quick patch: ```js
// client pseudo
client.set({tokenGraceMs:7000, resetConnOnRefresh:true, warmupRatePerSec:3, warmupJitterMs:250});
```
sam_dev: curious about the resetConnOnRefresh — will that make latency worse?
nina_sre: short-term yes, slightly higher latency on the first request after refresh due to new handshake, but avoids mid-stream 401s. It's better than whole request failing or retries. You can scope it to only reset when tokens are <= tokenGraceMs expiry.
sdk-bot: additional tip: for streaming endpoints, include a short keep-alive ping that re-validates token prior to sending big chunks. Something like: send small noop after refresh to confirm 200 before heavy payload.
ops-automation: @maria_cs I can temporarily bump tenant "zenfold" burst allowances +4rps for 48h to let them ramp without hitting 429s (change-id: B-99103). Want me to apply?
maria_cs: please apply the bump. Also @sam_dev if you can toggle resetConnOnRefresh in canary tomorrow, we can observe traces and metrics together.
sam_dev: applied the resetConnOnRefresh flag and lowered initial concurrency to 10 streams concurrently; added 200-400ms jitter on instance startup. We'll observe.
ops-automation: applied quota change for tenant "zenfold" (B-99103).
sam_dev: quick update after 20 min: mid-stream 401s dropped to zero and embedding 429s ceased during warmup. We'll keep the connection-reset flag for next 48h while we implement singleflight. Thanks all.
maria_cs: great news. I'll add a short entry in the onboarding playbook under "short TTL token patterns" with recommended SDK flags and the note about connection reuse. Also notifying renewals for the account health check-in.
nina_sre: follow-up item: we should add a server-side note to detect token rotation + connection reuse and return a clear header hint (e.g., "x-auth-stale:1") to make debugging easier. I'll open an infra ticket.
sam_dev: appreciated. We'll also capture our auth-proxy behavior and share it with you.
